ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, point D is on side $AB$, and points F, E are on side $AC$, with $DF \parallel BE$, $\frac{AF}{AE}=\frac{AE}{AC}$, and $DE\parallel BC$. Given $\frac{AF}{FE}=\frac{3}{2}$ and the area of $\triangle ABC$ is 12, find the value of the area of $\triangle ADE$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because \frac{AF}{FE}=\frac{3}{2}$,\\
$\therefore \frac{AD}{BD}=\frac{AF}{EF}=\frac{3}{2}$,\\
$\because DE\parallel BC$,\\
$\therefore \frac{AE}{CE}=\frac{AD}{BD}=\frac{3}{2}$,\\
$\therefore \frac{AE}{AC}=\frac{3}{5}$.\\
$\because DE\parallel BC$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ADE\sim \triangle ABC$.\\
$\therefore \frac{S_{\triangle ADE}}{S_{\triangle ABC}}=\left(\frac{AE}{AC}\right)^2=\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^2$, hence $\frac{S_{\triangle ADE}}{S_{\triangle ABC}}=\frac{9}{25}$,\\
$\because S_{\triangle ABC}=12$,\\
$\therefore \frac{S_{\triangle ADE}}{12}=\frac{9}{25}$, hence $S_{\triangle ADE}=\boxed{\frac{108}{25}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; point D is located on side AB, points F and E are located on side AC and F is above E; in the figure DF, DE, and BE are connected, among which DE is parallel to the base BC, and DF is parallel to BE. Reasoning: It is known that AF/FE=3/2. Since in triangle ABE, D is on AB, F is on AE, and DF ∥ BE, according to the theorem that parallel lines divide line segments proportionally, AD/DB=AF/FE=3/2. Also because in triangle ABC, DE ∥ BC, so AE/EC=AD/DB=3/2. Therefore AE/AC=3/(3+2)=3/5. From DE ∥ BC it can be known that triangle ADE and triangle ABC are similar, the linear ratio is AE/AC=3/5, so the area ratio is (3/5)^2=9/25. It is known that S_ABC=12, therefore S_ADE=12×9/25=108/25.
